answer: To prevent Sybil attacks, an AI agent economy employs a proof-of-work burn mechanism. Agents must verify their identity by expending computational tokens stored in a secure cryptographic vault. This deposit acts like a digital lantern, exposing malicious agent clusters. At the zenith of network activity, the high barrier of entry forces attackers to absorb unsustainable computational costs, rendering large-scale identity replication mathematically unviable.
